chapter: Race, revival and New Orleans jazz
title: Preservation Hall and the Dixieland revival
summary: Hug's mixed view of Preservation Hall's effect on the image of New Orleans music.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Right. What do you think of the current Dixieland revival? Do you think it's a healthy thing, the thing that's centered around Preservation Hall?

I think that the revival of Dixieland around Preservation Hall has been most fortunate for these musicians who hadn't played for so long. It gave them a chance to really get some work and it brought them out and some of them are real good musicians. However, I don't believe that this is just truly representative of just New Orleans musicians because you have so many musicians who played jazz, you know, I mean, Dixieland jazz and I believe a lot of people today hear Preservation Hall and they completely forget about any other type of Dixieland music which I don't really, I really don't like too much. I mean, this course, this is my personal opinion and as I said before, I'm not criticizing Preservation Hall musicians because there are many good ones and I think in general and in a whole I think that it's good for New Orleans because I think when people come here they go down there and they say, well, this is New Orleans music but there are a lot of other, what I'm getting at is that there is a lot of other good New Orleans music around.
